samples.question: This image shows one envelope lying at some angle on a page. The grey page frame and the four short grey ticks just inside it are fixed decoration: they never indicate the answer. The envelope is the large four-sided patch of paper. The big triangle printed on it is the envelope's flap, and the flap's straight base always runs along the envelope's own top edge, with the flap's point aimed at the middle of the envelope, however the envelope has been turned on the page. The small solid square patch is the stamp. The thin parallel strokes are address lines and never mark the answer. Turn the envelope in your mind, without flipping it over, until its flap base is at the top and its opposite edge is at the bottom; left and right mean your left and right in that upright view, so they are not the left and right of the page. The stamp belongs to the corner that contains the centre of the stamp. The colours, the size and shape of the envelope, where it sits on the page, the angle it is turned through, the size of the stamp and the number and placement of the address lines all change from image to image, and the stamp need not be placed where a stamp is normally placed. Read only what is painted in this image and do not answer from where stamps usually go. In which corner of the envelope is the stamp? Answer with exactly one of: top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right.
